notes.text: UAE property is bought mostly with cash: Dubai Land Department data show 83.4% of residential transactions in 2024 were non-mortgaged, and 60% of transaction value in Abu Dhabi was non-mortgaged. Direct residential lending was only 4.6% of banks' gross loans in 2024, so the policy rate, which tracks the US Federal Reserve under the dirham peg, has limited direct traction on prices; liquidity and capital inflows matter more.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/327)

notes.text: Central Bank of the UAE rules cap loan-to-value at 85% for UAE nationals' first homes, 65% for subsequent properties and 50% for off-plan purchases, with higher down payments for expatriates and for homes above AED 5 million; debt-burden ratios are capped at 60% of gross salary for nationals and 50% for expatriates, loans at 8 and 7 years of income respectively, and tenors at 25 years (as described by the IMF in December 2025). The off-plan cap limits bank financing of speculative presales.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/327)

notes.text: Dubai prices rose 117.6% for villas and 46.2% for apartments between 2020Q1 and 2025Q2, driven by population and non-oil growth, international investors and structural reforms such as golden visas; the IMF estimates real house prices are above trend, with the cycle tracking non-oil GDP and liquidity. In Abu Dhabi, buyers living outside the UAE rose from 4% of sales value in 2019 to 16% in 2024, and 81% of units are renter-occupied, making the market investor-driven.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/327)

notes.text: The UAE grants a five-year golden residence visa to real estate investors with minimum capital of AED 2 million, tying residency to property ownership and sustaining foreign demand for higher-value units.

sources.publisher: The United Arab Emirates' Government portal (u.ae)

notes.text: Dubai's planned completions are expected to jump to about 83,000 units in 2026 and 99,000 in 2027, against 29,000 delivered in 2024, which the IMF says could help balance demand; however, only 62% of units planned for 2025 had been delivered by October 31, 2025, so actual handovers usually fall short of plans. In Abu Dhabi, off-plan projects made up 74% of sales value in 2024.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/327)

notes.text: The headline price series and projections for the UAE use the BIS detailed residential property price series for all dwellings, which runs from 2014 to 2023, so the outlook starts from a dated base. Dubai's own quarterly residential price index, from Dubai Real Estate Data, an independent platform built on Dubai Land Department open data and rebased to 2020 = 100, appears at city level and is more current, but it covers Dubai only and not Abu Dhabi or the other emirates.
